data.description:
## Problem

smiling-ancient-finwhale (2e85d8558a4) heals a reclaim-superseded clone on `append_event`, `transition_core` and `claim_core`: the write precheck raises `SupersededStoreRefused`, the writer runs one `sync.reconverge` with the write lock free, and retries once. Every other writer still refuses a superseded clone, so on a clone that has already fetched a reclaimed baseline these operations fail until an unthrottled read or idle-sync round happens to move it:

- `rebar delete` (`_commands/delete.py::delete_cli`)
- NDJSON import (`_io/import_ndjson.py::import_tickets` → `_flush`, which calls `_seam._refuse_unpublishable_store` directly)
- a reconciler pass (`reconciler/inbound_translate.py::_write_event_file` → `finalize_event`)
- the atomic completion close, and with it every gate that probes store freshness before it decides: `close_precheck` → `freshness.assert_gate_store_fresh` (completion close), `llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py::claim_gate_check` (plan-review claim gate), `_commands/gates.py::close_plan_review_gate_check` (plan-review close gate) and `llm/plan_review/__init__.py::_stale_store_verdict` (review-plan). `freshness.store_freshness` reports a superseded clone as `diverged`, so these return `stale-store` before any write is reached. This also means a claim with the plan-review gate on is still refused on a superseded clone, which the landed fix does not cover.

## Cause (reproduced)

Reproduced at origin/main 2e85d8558a4 in `tests/interfaces/store/test_write_after_reclaim_other_paths.py` (real bare origin; a parentless baseline whose lineage names the clone's epoch is published and fetched; the read-path throttle marker is stamped as just-run): delete exits 1 with "ticket write refused … DIVERGED"; `import_tickets` raises `SupersededStoreRefused` at the first flush; a guarded reconciler pass whose reconcile step writes one inbound event writes nothing (`_write_event_file` raises the refusal); `assert_gate_store_fresh` raises "the completion close gate refused to certify … DIVERGED"; `claim_gate_check` returns verdict `stale-store`. None of these writers or gates calls the heal.

## Approach

One heal, `freshness.heal_superseded_clone` (the existing `sync.reconverge` round: fetch, take the write lock, `_override_if_reclaimed`), reached in the way each path's locking allows.

- **delete — heal-and-retry.** `delete_cli` holds no write lock and its write phase already rolls back every file it wrote on `CommandError`. Move the resolve-through-commit phase into one function wrapped in `_seam.retry_after_superseded_heal`; the rollback re-raises `SupersededStoreRefused` so the wrapper heals and retries the whole phase (ticket resolution and child check included).
- **NDJSON import — heal-and-retry at the flush precheck.** Events are buffered in memory and nothing is staged before `_flush`, so `_flush` runs its existing precheck through `retry_after_superseded_heal`; the chunk is then committed on the reclaimed baseline.
- **reconciler pass — heal before the pass, not retry.** A mid-pass heal is unsafe: by the time an inbound event is written, the pass has already made outbound Jira mutations (so the pass cannot be retried), and it holds uncommitted inbound event files and binding-state edits in the tracker working tree until `pass_support._commit_binding_store_snapshot` commits them at pass end; the override's `reset --hard` would discard tracked edits and leave the pass's files on a different base. So `reconciler/guarded_pass.py::run_pass_result` heals a proven-superseded clone before `reconcile_once` (one probe per pass, through `write_blocking_divergence`'s `superseded` flag), skipped for the read-only `preview` route. A clone superseded mid-pass is still refused by the unchanged precheck.
- **store-freshness gates (completion close, plan-review claim/close gates, review-plan) — heal-and-reprobe.** `freshness.store_freshness`, when its verdict is `diverged`, checks whether the fetched remote supersedes the clone; if so and the store write lock is free (`lock.write_lock_is_busy`), it runs the heal and re-probes. It never waits for the lock: the plan-review close gate's locked recheck (`transition_close._plan_review_close_recheck`, run inside `transition_core`'s lock) sees a busy lock and reports exactly as today. A `behind` store is still not adopted by a gate; only a lineage-proven supersession is moved. The completion verifier therefore reads the healed store and its receipt pins the healed tickets OID.
- **atomic completion close itself — cannot use heal-and-retry (evidence).** `completion_bundle.commit_completion_bundle` validates a receipt pinned to the tickets OID the verifier read; `_snapshot/ticket_receipt.py::validate_receipt` refuses with `non_ancestor_tickets_history` unless that OID is an ancestor of HEAD, and the override resets onto an unrelated history, so any close retried after a heal is refused by design. `completion_txn` is left unchanged; the gate heal above runs before the verifier, which is the point where healing is sound. A clone superseded between the gate and the commit is still refused, and a re-run of the close heals at the gate.
- No new config key, env var or flag. The refusal type stays a `CommandError` subclass, so existing error handling is unchanged.

## Scope

In: `src/rebar/_commands/delete.py`, `src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py`, `src/rebar/reconciler/guarded_pass.py`, `src/rebar/_store/freshness.py`, `docs/concurrency.md`, `tests/interfaces/store/reclaim_harness.py` (shared fixture, moved out of the existing test module), `tests/interfaces/store/test_write_after_reclaim.py` (now imports the harness) and the new `tests/interfaces/store/test_write_after_reclaim_other_paths.py`. Out: `completion_txn.py` and `completion_bundle.py` (unchanged, reason above); a clone whose remote-tracking ref has not been fetched yet (not superseded from the local view; its next sync round moves it).

## Testing

`tests/interfaces/store/test_write_after_reclaim_other_paths.py`, same harness as the landed tests:
- delete, import, reconciler pass: on a superseded clone the write lands on the reclaimed baseline (delete's STATUS and import's CREATE are on the remote tip above the baseline; the pass's inbound event file exists and HEAD descends from the baseline). Against a remote whose lineage names another epoch: refused as DIVERGED, clone HEAD and working tree unchanged, remote unchanged, nothing written.
- gates: `assert_gate_store_fresh` (completion close gate) and `claim_gate_check` pass on a superseded clone and leave HEAD on the reclaimed lineage; the completion close gate still refuses an unrelated remote.
- heal failure: with the fetch failing, and with the write lock held by another holder (heal lock wait shortened to 1 s), a comment on a superseded clone that holds an unpushed local event is refused as DIVERGED; HEAD, the working tree, the unpushed event and the remote are unchanged and no stale-override backup ref exists.

All superseded-path tests fail on 2e85d8558a4 (5 fail there today: delete, import, reconciler, completion close gate, claim gate). Existing `test_write_after_reclaim.py`, `test_stale_clone_override.py`, `test_gate_store_freshness.py`, `test_fsck_push_pending.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py`, the import suites under `tests/interfaces/io/` and `tests/unit/reconciler/` stay green, then `make verify`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a clone a reclaim superseded (remote lineage names the local epoch, remote ref already fetched), `rebar delete`, an NDJSON import and a reconciler pass each succeed and write on top of the reclaimed baseline; regression tests prove each and fail on 2e85d8558a4.
- [ ] On such a clone the completion-close store-freshness gate and the plan-review claim gate move the clone and do not report `stale-store`; regression tests prove both and fail on 2e85d8558a4. The atomic completion commit itself is left unchanged for the receipt-ancestry reason recorded in the Approach.
- [ ] Against a remote whose lineage does not name the local epoch, delete, import, the reconciler pass and the completion-close gate are still refused as DIVERGED and write nothing.
- [ ] A heal that fails (failed fetch; write lock held by another holder) leaves the write refused as DIVERGED and loses no event: HEAD, the working tree, an unpushed local event and the remote are unchanged, and no stale-override backup ref is created.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.
data.title: Other writers refuse a clone a reclaim superseded
